texts: good. the approach, the lit lantern and its position on the West Row are all carried; note only that "day 121 of Year 1" lands on a day-of-month term, so a day-of-year count has no distinct reading for the translator — a coverage gap no rewrite avoids.
good. the draining takes the wraith as agent, mire-essence as what is drawn off and the lantern of the previous sentence as the source, and "mire-essence" is decomposed to its essence genus.

bad: "for the rest of the night" has no carrier — it comes out as an end-point atom saying the giving stopped when night came, roughly the opposite of its lasting the night out, and "the rest of" is dropped outright. Name the endpoint as a time the translator can take: "The drained lantern gave weak mist-light until dawn."
good. the mist-light resolves back to the previous sentence, and the moths come through as a group with "a handful" recorded verbatim as a vague-count phrase.
good. the persistence is reified with the wraith as its subject and an eleven-day duration, which is what the later "during its persistence" adjuncts attach to.

good. the six-lantern group, its count, its position on the row and its containment in the persistence are all carried. Two things worth knowing: the lanterns are the direct object here, whereas sentence 2 made the day-121 lantern the source of a draining, so nothing links that first lantern into this group of six; and no per-lantern rule is emitted, so a single lantern named later is not derivably one of the drained ones.

good. it becomes a fireable per-lantern rule — a counting event, the keepers, a moth group, the lantern as location and the persistence as the containing period. "about six" is kept verbatim as a count phrase, so the hedge is preserved but will not convert to a numeric bound downstream; and because the rule ranges over the group of six, the lantern of sentences 1-3 falls outside "each drained lantern".

bad: "that week" has no antecedent anywhere in the passage, and the parse silently resolves it to the eleven-day persistence — a containment you never stated; "sharply" is dropped too, since a degree adverb on a verb has no slot. Name the period and carry the degree as a predicate: "The thread harvest at the West Row fell during the wraith's persistence, and the fall was sharp."
good. the row is typed and named, decomposed to its row genus, and both positions — on the Cliff Path, near the Sunken Cove — keep their own prepositions rather than being flattened into containment.
